canonical_topic: Types of underground gas storage sites
definition: Three geological formations are used for natural gas storage — depleted gas reservoirs, converted salt caverns, and aquifers — chosen based on what is available in a given area.
core_idea: Depleted reservoirs are the cheapest and most reliable option, salt caverns deliver the best performance because they tolerate much higher pressure, and aquifers (water-bearing permeable rock) are used only where the other two options aren't available.
key_points: Depleted gas reservoirs: cheapest, most reliable.
Converted salt caverns: highest performance, able to withstand significantly higher pressure than the alternatives.
Aquifers: permeable rock layers often containing groundwater, used as a fallback option.
Choice of storage type in a region is generally limited to whatever geology is locally available.
relationships: Salt cavern performance advantage ties directly to the maximum-pressure constraint discussed above.
